claim: spec/emit/arch_resolver.md's "Parent Resolution" section (lines 62-64): "If the journal holds no registered event for the proposal, that is an emit error naming the slug: registration opens the lifecycle, so the fix is `spex register`, not a synthesized epic." This requires Resolver to distinguish, for a proposal slug with no live epic task, two states — "never registered" (error) versus "registered, epic task not yet created" (synthesize a new epic, ref:op) — using only the journal fold.
authoritative_source: spec/emit/arch_resolver.md's own "Interface" section (lines 96-98): "the fold is an equally narrow surface: node key in, latest task-bearing pairing out" — and spec/map/arch_mapping_store.md's "Responsibilities" (line 14) and "Interface" (line 86): "ask for the fold and receive one entry per task-bearing node — hash, current task id, and the sourcing event." A proposal that carries only a `registered` event with no `task_created` receipt referencing it is, by this contract, not task-bearing and yields no fold entry at all — the same miss a never-registered proposal produces.
evidence: mapping.MappingStore's fold() (map/mapping_store.go, implementing arch_mapping_store.md's contract exactly) only ever writes an `entries[proposal]` record inside the `task_created` case, keyed off a `registered` event it finds by eid — never inside the `registered` case itself. So `Fold.Entry("<slug>")` returns `ok=false` identically whether the slug was never registered or was registered five minutes ago with the epic task not yet created. Resolver's own "Interface" section confirms this is not an oversight to patch around locally: the fold is documented as answering task-bearing pairings only, nothing else, which forecloses a `Registered(slug) bool`-shaped read through that surface. The only other MappingStore read that could answer it, Parse() (raw events, including `registered` lines), is not one of the three inputs arch_resolver.md's Interface section lists Resolver as being "set up with" (spec graph, journal fold, batch map), and no sibling component (ChangesetBuilder, EmitCommand) exposes it to Resolver either — checked map/mapping_store.go, cmd/spex/emit.go's journalFold adapter (wraps mapping.Fold only), and emit/builder.go's hasExistingEpic (also `Fold.Entry` only). test_changeset_builder.md's "Proposal epic parents every non-epic create" scenario (lines 39-41) requires exactly this distinguishing behavior as an assertable Builder.Build() error, so the gap is not hypothetical — it blocks writing a passing test for a scenario this bead's own test leaf specifies.
proposed_fix: Give the journal fold a way to answer registration independent of task-bearing status — e.g. widen map's fold to also emit a FoldEntry for a `registered` event with no `task_created` yet (TaskID empty, a new Registered/EID-bearing flag, overwritten in-place if a task_created for it appears later), and update arch_mapping_store.md's Responsibilities/Interface text (currently 'one entry per task-bearing node') to describe the widened contract. Then thread that capability into emit.JournalFold (a second narrow method, e.g. `Registered(proposal string) (eid string, ok bool)`) and update arch_resolver.md's Interface section to list it as a fourth narrow read alongside the other three, so Resolver.ResolveParent can return the no-registered-event error itself instead of silently falling through to "synthesize a new epic" the way Builder's current hasExistingEpic() does.
